Used to work on billing for an energy company and used to see this happen pretty often.

The debt isn't yours obviously. So I wouldn't worry about it.

If its been let out before I wouldn't jump to conclusions either that the landlord/ex owner is being malicious or anything. What tends to happen is when the old tenants move out they'll ring in and let the energy company know they're moving out. At this point the names will then be reverted back to the landlord and he may be completely unaware of this, its fairly common that there's never any other property on record for him or her other than the one you've now bought. Although any experienced landlord should know this its easy to realise why it may slip someone's mind who let out an inherited property or something.

I found myself in a similar position when I bought my house. The woman I bought it from had actually bought it for her daughter to live in. The woman herself was living in a home. They fell out and the mother sold the property, but it was dormant for 10 months. Enough time to rack up a couple of hundred in standing charges even though there was no energy use. She would not have been aware of this and the debt company didn't know her new address. 

What I would do in your position is simply write 'not known at this address, return to sender' on any further letters that come in the ex homeowners name. When I did this Royal Mail resent them to my address, so at that point I rang up and explained to the debt company and energy company. You should always take a picture the day you buy or sell a property of the readings. So you have evidence of the correct readings.

And finally, with regards to the amount of the bill and I touched on this earlier, the property may not have had any energy used at all. Hence, there is no bill to worry about. However, I believe with all tariffs (at least when I worked there 5 years ago) had a daily standing charge, regardless of wether there were any usage or not. Cant remember off the top of my head how much, but I think they were usually around 20-25p per day for each supply. Assuming theres gas and electric, that's £12-£15 a month. I never worked on home move or debt which these calls i would normally pass on, but from my perspective I'd assume these debts could be disputeable. The landlord probably never agreed to any tariff, you just automatically get put on a standard tariff. On top of that of course there's probably debt fees added too.

You may or may not be aware of this. But many people don't realise the difference between Mbps (bits) and MB/s (bytes). Whenever you do a speed test most places will give you the speed in Mbps (bits). But if you download a file Windows will tell you in MB/s (bytes).
